variants.name: kotlinx.coroutines Flow: suspending emit + buffer/conflate
variants.implementation_notes: In Kotlin backpressure is a property of suspension rather than of a queue: a cold Flow's emitter runs in the collector's coroutine, so emit suspends until the consumer is ready and `flow { }.collect { }` cannot overflow - the classic bounded queue is replaced by structured suspension. buffer(n)/buffer(Channel.BUFFERED) inserts an explicit channel stage that suspends the producer once it is full, conflate keeps only the newest value (DROP_OLDEST, never suspending upstream, so it is lossy on purpose), and collectLatest cancels the previous downstream computation instead of queueing. Choose conflate/collectLatest only when 'latest wins' is the true semantics; for messages that must all be processed, the plain sequential flow plus a bounded buffer is correct.
pitfalls: buffer(Channel.UNLIMITED) or an unbounded Channel removes the bound and recreates the memory problem it was supposed to prevent.
conflate()/collectLatest() silently drop or cancel work - only valid for state that is 'latest wins', not for commands.
flowOn changes the dispatcher of upstream operators only; a blocking call in the collector still stalls the consumer.
A hot SharedFlow is paced by its shared buffer and onBufferOverflow policy, not by each collector, so a slow subscriber is buffered or dropped rather than slowing the emitter.

variants.name: Bounded Channel hand-off between independent coroutines
variants.idiom_name: Channel(capacity = n) with suspending send / trySend
variants.implementation_notes: For a hot hand-off between independent producers and consumers the explicit form is a bounded Channel: Channel<T>(capacity = n) with send() suspending when full, trySend() giving the non-blocking shed path (ChannelResult), and receive() suspending when empty. The classic queue is replaced by the channel's internal buffer plus coroutine suspension, and the same capacity tokens appear everywhere (RENDEZVOUS, BUFFERED, CONFLATED, UNLIMITED, or a number) so the full policy must be chosen deliberately. callbackFlow/channelFlow adapt push APIs (listeners, callbacks) into this demand-aware model, with awaitClose as the cleanup hook.
pitfalls: Channel.UNLIMITED is an unbounded queue with extra steps; Channel.BUFFERED is a fixed internal default, not 'whatever the workload needs'.
A channel must be closed by its producer; forgetting close() leaves consumers suspended forever.
send() on a full channel suspends the coroutine - if the producer and consumer share a single-threaded dispatcher the pipeline deadlocks.
trySend() failures are silently ignored unless handled, which converts backpressure into invisible data loss.
